research_question: What is the effect of personalised psychological interventions (standard interventions adapted or developed for a specific subgroup of children with conduct problems), compared with non-personalised (standard) interventions, on child conduct problems measured by the Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory (ECBI) Problem subscale in the short term (one month post-intervention or less) in children with conduct problems?
outcome_description: Child conduct problems assessed by the Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory (ECBI) Problem subscale at post-intervention or short-term follow-up (≤ 1 month post-intervention)
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates greater reduction in child conduct problems (greater improvement favoring the personalised intervention) compared to the standard intervention
search_queries: personalised parent training conduct problems trial
adapted intervention child disruptive behavior ECBI randomized controlled
tailored psychological intervention children conduct problems comparison outcome
inclusion_criteria: Empirical studies of children with conduct problems receiving a personalised or adapted psychological intervention compared with a standard, non-personalised active intervention
Quantitative assessment of child conduct problems using the Eyberg Child Behavior Inventory (ECBI) Problem subscale at post-intervention or short-term follow-up (one month or less)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, theoretical papers, and case reports are excluded)
No direct comparison between a personalised (adapted/subgroup-targeted) intervention and a standard (non-personalised) psychological intervention
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (means and SDs, sample sizes, change scores, or test statistics)
Completely unrelated to psychological interventions in children with conduct problems
moderators_to_extract: Subgroup adaptation target (e.g., callous-unemotional traits, comorbid ADHD, child age)
Base intervention model (e.g., Parent-Child Interaction Therapy, Triple P, Incredible Years)
Delivery format (individual vs. group parent training)
Child mean age and gender distribution
effect_size_note: Because higher scores on the ECBI Problem scale reflect greater problem severity, effect sizes should be coded such that positive values indicate greater symptom reduction (greater benefit) for the personalised intervention relative to standard intervention.
